dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: Q3 26: revenue $4.69-4.77B (+15-17% YoY, incl. ~3pts FX TAILWIND after hedging); GBV growth mid-teens (nights & seats low double-digit, ADR up moderately on mix and price); adjusted EBITDA up YoY but margin slightly below Q3-25 (investment timing); no Middle East impact assumed.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 RAISED: revenue growth now 'at least mid-teens' (from low-to-mid teens) and adjusted EBITDA margin >=35.5% (from 35%); implied take rate roughly flat (RNPL booking-to-stay timing + new-business incentives; slightly up without them).
pointsCles: Q2 26 beat across every key metric: revenue $3.61B (+17%, above the high end), GBV $27.2B (+16%), nights & seats +10% (accelerating); GAAP EPS $1.37 beat by $0.13 but includes a $77M one-off tax benefit (~$0.13/share, bridged in quarterlyEPS - recurring base ~$1.24); adjusted EBITDA $1.3B at 35% margin (+100bp), TTM FCF $4.8B (37% margin), $1.1B buybacks.

Breadth is the story: first-time bookers +11% (best in 4 years, Gen Z fastest), app nights 64% of total (+23%), expansion markets ~2x core AND core re-accelerating (US, France, UK, Australia); RNPL >20% of GBV and extended; single service fee on ~half of listings, full rollout by year-end.

Hotels growing ~3x faster than homes (single-digit % of nights): inbound supply interest flipped positive, top-20 city rollout, and ~35% of first-time hotel guests come back to book a home - hotels feed homes; services expand via partnerships (car rentals biggest, reservation length > stay length; luggage storage a sleeper hit) with little cost carried by Airbnb.

AI-native rebuild pays: concept-to-launch -60%, features shipped +80%, support cost per booking -16% (AI assistant resolves ~45% without a human, voice later this year), AI search entering opt-in tests this month, new AI host-pricing model called 'many multiples bigger than RNPL' as a growth lever; FY guidance absorbs materially higher AI spend while RAISING margin.

ancrages.moteur: FY26 guidance raised a SECOND time on the Q2'26 call: revenue growth targeted at 'at least mid-teens' (~15,5% central case retained, vs '~14%' at the previous refresh) - consistent with the actual Q1->Q2 acceleration (revenue +18% then +17% YoY on a tougher base) and the Q3 guidance (revenue guided +15% to +17% YoY); gradual 2027-2030 deceleration unchanged in shape, rebased on this new 2026 starting point.

FY26 Adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to >=35,5% (vs >=35% previously); bottom-up reconstruction from the actual quarters (Q1/Q2 26 actuals + Q3 guide, bearing in mind that Q3 concentrates the bulk of annual profitability - Adjusted EBITDA margin of 50% in Q3 2025 alone, against 34-35% at a normal run rate) implies a FY26 GAAP EBIT margin of ~27,9% - materially higher than the previous flat estimate (21,5%), which understated the operating leverage of Q3. 2027-2030 trajectory rebased proportionally, with the margin continuing to expand gradually towards ~32,4% in 2030 (recovery/scaling of the new verticals).

Rule E5-a bis, case 3: negative net debt (net cash ~9,5 Md$ at end-FY25) and an active, regular buyback programme documented since 2022 (10,9 Md$ repurchased, 6 Md$ authorisation opened in February 2024, run rate ~3,8-4 Md$/yr) -> projected net financial income of 0% (cash treated as consumed by buybacks during the year). See PARAMETERS for the discussion of the bias this choice introduces on this specific stock (net cash far above the annual buyback run rate, ~700-800 M$/yr of actual interest observed in FY24-FY25).

Normative effective tax rate set at 20%, based on the actual effective rates of FY2024 (20,5%) and FY2025 (19,95%), both clean (after the FY2023 tax one-off adjusted out via E5 d-bis) and mutually consistent.

Diluted share count reduction projected at ~3%/yr, moderated vs the exceptional FY2025 pace (-3,4%, 623M vs 645M), consistent with the 6 Md$ buyback authorisation opened in February 2024 and the capital-return priority reaffirmed by management.

Issuance of 2,5 Md$ of senior notes in Q1'26 (investment grade ratings obtained), used to repay the 2,0 Md$ of 0% convertibles due in 2026 - raises gross debt by around 0,5 Md$. Net debt (net cash) projected broadly stable to slightly less negative over the horizon (buybacks consuming most of the annual free cash flow generated), rather than a trajectory of net cash growing without limit.

hypothese.summary: Global leader in short-term rentals in the middle of a platform extension (experiences, hotel pilots, services), Q1'26 revenue +18% YoY and FY26 guidance raised (growth 'low to mid teens', Adjusted EBITDA margin >=35%). Marked and documented gap vs consensus: the Omnium omniumEPS is built on projected net financial income of 0% (rule E5-a bis, net cash treated as consumed by the active buybacks), whereas the stock actually generates ~700-800 M$/yr of recurring financial interest - a conservative bias knowingly accepted, to be revisited at the next refresh.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Airbnb is the dominant short-stay platform with growing optionality in experiences and hotel pilots (NY, LA, SF, Madrid). The bet: sustained double-digit revenue growth (FY26 guidance upgraded twice, now 'at least mid-teens'), a massive continuous buyback (10.9bn$ retired since 2022; ~3%/yr share shrink modeled) and AI-driven cost discipline compound into steady operating-margin expansion. The methodological signature of this file is deliberate: E5 a-bis Option A is applied to the letter - the ~9.5bn$ net cash pile really earns 700-800M$/yr of interest, but the model projects that at ZERO (cash treated as consumed by buybacks), so the projected 80% Net/EBIT conversion sits far below the published 114% (2025: real interest + ~9% GAAP tax). That conservatism is assumed, documented, and flagged for periodic re-discussion rather than smoothed - it is the main reason W1 flags this file, by design.

== THESIS READ ==
- FY26 revenue guidance upgraded a second time (at least mid-teens): the demand engine keeps outrunning the plan set in February.
- Q2 above the top of guidance with Middle-East drag absorbed - the Q1 'fragility' read was conjunctural, as management claimed.
- Buyback pace (~3.8-4bn$/yr) against 9.5bn$ net cash: Option A's zero-interest assumption stays a deliberate ~0.90$/share EPS haircut vs economic reality.
- Experiences/hotels pilots still unquantified in revenue - optionality, not yet a driver.
- Watch: the FY25 'clean' tax rate looked closer to 13% than the 20% normative - reconcile at the FY26 close (could be a structural EPS tailwind if confirmed).

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
None.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: published US GAAP. Bridge (c-ter): projections at exactly t=20% (ancrage etr_normatif_20pct) and finNet=0 (ancrage netfin_zero_buyback, Option A) - the chain reconciles to the cent; the published 2025 year reconciles at +450M$ interest and ~9% effective tax, which fully explains the W1 conversion gap (114% -> 80%), by construction not by error. Shares -3%/yr (buyback_pace_3pct); ND barely declining (cash generation offset by buybacks). Scorecard: quarterly revenue guider - FY26 anchor own_vintage 3.97$ (22/07, pre-upgrades, low baseline), history not measurable at setup, application suspended (documented). WATCH-LIST: (1) Option A re-discussion trigger: any material change in cash/buyback profile; (2) FY25 clean tax ~13% vs 20% normative - reconcile at FY26 close; (3) hotels/experiences first quantified contribution; (4) buyback pace post debt refinancing. Next useful refresh: Q3 results (early November).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 2026 (early Nov): third guidance touchpoint of the year; experiences/hotel pilots metrics; buyback cadence.

clesRetenues: Q Justin Post (BofA) - progress of the hotels initiative in cities that are already well supplied (not only markets constrained by regulation): management confirms a reception far above expectations on both sides (hotels AND unconstrained markets), ~35% of first-time hotel bookers come back to book a home.

Q Richard Clarke (Bernstein) - ultimate ambition for the ancillary products (simple attach vs full OTA) and impact of Expedia's acquisition of partner CarTrawler on the M&A strategy: the CEO describes 3 phases (current attach -> one-stop travel shop -> beyond travel), confirms his confidence in the continuation of the CarTrawler partnership despite the acquisition, reaffirms an opportunistic M&A strategy with no increased urgency.

Q Lloyd Walmsley (Mizuho) - markets where the improvement in hotel conversion is most visible and timing of the AI search tests: rollout extended to about twenty cities, selective hotel inventory (complementary, not competing with homes); AI tests start this month on a small share of traffic via an optional toggle, progressive extension over the year depending on results.

Q Jed Kelly (Oppenheimer) - whether the single service fee will be extended to all hosts or stays limited to professional property managers: migration under way to the entire host base, completion expected before year-end (about half of active listings already migrated).

Q Ken Gawrelski (Wells Fargo) - reaction of legacy hosts to the arrival of hotels on the platform and geo-by-geo vs global approach to trip planning: very little negative feedback from core hosts, analogy with the Amazon flywheel effect (a new category does not cannibalise, it strengthens the existing one); supply (hotels/services/experiences) tested city by city, but global trip planning will be rolled out globally.

Q Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs) - trade-off between reinvestment and long-term recovery in incremental margin: the CFO declines a quantified guide beyond 2026, confirms a structural floor of capacity to invest while still delivering margin expansion, and points to the recent track record as the best available indicator.

Q Ron Josey (Citi) - detail of the host pricing tools and current contribution of experiences to nights booked: pricing is presented as the largest growth lever available (far more than Reserve Now Pay Later), a new AI-driven pricing model is being rolled out; experiences still at small scale, a multi-year contribution horizon explicitly accepted (not this year).

Q John Colantuoni (Jefferies) - impact of the AI-native transition on product costs and operational adjustments: the CEO plays down the cost impact (marginal inference costs against the ROI of high-value transactions), the CFO nevertheless confirms a material increase already built into guidance for AI spend, partly offset by the decline in customer support cost (-16% YoY) and headcount growth slower than in the past.

Q Kevin Kopelman (TD Cowen) - drivers of the acceleration in first-time bookers (+11%, highest level in 4 years): attributed to the cumulative effect of multiple product improvements rather than to a single factor, particular strength in India/Brazil (expansion markets) AND a recent acceleration in the core markets (including the US); Reserve Now Pay Later explicitly cited as a conversion factor for hesitant new users.

Q Conor Cunningham (Melius Research) - breakdown of the quarter's growth acceleration and long-term pricing strategy on ADR: management declines to isolate a single factor (points to a list of 12-15 improvements in the shareholder letter), specifies that the rise in ADR partly reflects the growing popularity of large family homes (more bedrooms, a genuine mix effect) and not solely a nominal price increase.

Q Colin Sebastian (Baird) - which new service categories show the strongest traction/unit economics and the pace of investment: car rental cited as the biggest opportunity (booking duration above expectations), luggage storage cited as an unexpected success ('sleeper hit'); most additional services operate through PARTNERSHIP (low marginal cost as it is borne by the partner), management does not expect a significant increase in the costs tied to this expansion.

Q Doug Anmuth (JPMorgan) - a more formal B2B opportunity over time: the CEO explicitly rules out white label, favours a 'consumer-first' strategy (Apple vs BlackBerry analogy) in which enterprise adoption follows consumer adoption rather than the reverse - B2B strategy described as 'emerging', with no quantified commitment or timeline given.
